title: fix: ignore caller tools on managed agents instead of rejecting
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Managed agents 400'd on any request carrying `tools`. Open WebUI injects builtin tool specs into **every** chat sent from its UI (`use_builtin_tools` defaults on for any session; connection-fetched models have no `meta.capabilities` to disable it), so 100% of agent calls from Open WebUI failed with `Caller-provided tools are not supported by managed agents`.
- Observed on 3 agents / 3 users in the first day of openwebui.pollinations.ai. No user configuration involved — the tools are Open WebUI's own builtins, not the Pollinations MCP tool server.
- An agent runs its own tools, so caller tools were never going to be used. Dropping them is no more lossy than erroring, and non-fatal.
- `tool_choice` and `parallel_tool_calls` keep rejecting — Open WebUI sends neither.

gist.headline: Tools enter, quietly exit
gist.blurb: Managed agents now wave past Open WebUI’s automatic tool bundle instead of stopping at the door. The agents already have their own toolbox; no need for the lobby to get crowded.
gist.summary: Managed-agent requests now ignore caller-provided `tools` while continuing to reject unsupported `tool_choice` and `parallel_tool_calls`, allowing Open WebUI’s automatically injected builtin tools to coexist with agent chats.
gist.impact: Open WebUI users can now send chats to managed agents normally even when the UI includes its default builtin tool specs, restoring calls that previously returned HTTP 400.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy agent workshop: Polli gently places an oversized stack of caller tool cards into a clearly labeled “not needed” compost bin while a happy managed-agent terminal uses its own small tool belt. The visual metaphor is harmlessly filtering Open WebUI’s automatic tools rather than rejecting the whole chat, with sprouting code-plants showing the request continuing onward.
